episode.title: Preserve an explicitly selected credential profile over ambient access keys
episode.before: At parent 04b15259b216294038169664aa4782d777b0281f, the runtime client set its profile from either an explicit option or the environment-aware profile lookup, then independently copied any resolved access-key pair into config.credentials. Consequently, when the authentication flow supplied a stored/scoped profile while ambient AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY were present, the explicit credentials field overrode the selected profile in the SDK client.
episode.after: At b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89, the runtime distinguishes an explicitly selected or stored/scoped profile from an ambient profile. It still places the selected profile in the client configuration, but only injects an access-key pair when authentication is enabled, a complete pair exists, and no explicit/scoped profile was selected. Ambient access keys remain available when there is no authoritative profile, including when AWS_PROFILE itself is only ambient.
episode.diff: The implementation adds optionsProfile = options.profile || options.env?.AWS_PROFILE, uses it before the general environment-aware profile lookup, and adds !optionsProfile to the access-key injection guard. A new mocked client-configuration test suite covers explicit profile plus ambient keys, scoped profile plus ambient keys, keys without a profile, and keys with only an ambient profile. The commit changes one implementation file and adds one 115-line test file (123 insertions, 2 deletions).

evidence_units.claim: Commit b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89 is the implementation-bearing resolution, has parent 04b15259b216294038169664aa4782d777b0281f, changes the runtime credential configuration and adds credential-priority tests, and states that explicit credentials were overriding the profile selected through the authentication flow.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit, parent_commit, commit_show_stat, and changed_files_name_status

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, profile resolution and access-key injection were independent: config.profile used options.profile or the environment-aware AWS_PROFILE lookup, while every complete access-key pair was assigned to config.credentials whenever skip-auth was false.

The change introduces a separate optionsProfile value sourced only from the explicit profile option or scoped option environment, retains the broader lookup as a fallback for config.profile, and prevents access-key injection when optionsProfile is present.
evidence_units.source: git diff 04b15259b216294038169664aa4782d777b0281f b63403a50f57fa0e3098684e927a63279598ec89 -- packages/ai/src/api/bedrock-converse-stream.ts; resulting lines 134-142 and 192-195

evidence_units.claim: The provider-owned login flow stores an entered profile as credential.env.AWS_PROFILE, and authentication resolution returns that scoped environment with stored-credential provenance.

The model execution layer merges provider-resolved environment values into request options before invoking the provider stream, allowing a stored profile to arrive at the runtime as options.env.AWS_PROFILE.

The regression test passes an explicit profile and then a scoped AWS_PROFILE while ambient access keys are set; both resulting client configurations retain the selected profile and omit config.credentials.
The fallback test verifies that a complete ambient access-key pair is copied into config.credentials when no profile is configured.
The provenance-boundary test verifies that an ambient AWS_PROFILE does not suppress ambient access keys: both config.profile and config.credentials are populated.

The test harness mocks the runtime client, captures its constructor configuration through the public compatibility stream call, and asserts exactly one client construction, providing a direct oracle for credential-selection output without making a provider request.

candidate_atomics.name: classify-authoritative-profile-source
candidate_atomics.title: Distinguish an authoritative profile choice from ambient profile discovery
candidate_atomics.description: Derive a profile marker only from request-explicit or stored/scoped configuration, while retaining ambient profile discovery solely as the client profile fallback. This preserves source provenance for the later credential-precedence decision.

semantic_action.intent: Identify when a profile represents a deliberate request or stored authentication choice that must outrank ambient access keys.
semantic_action.module_role: Credential-source precedence resolver at the provider client boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: Profile lookup collapses explicit, stored/scoped, and ambient profile sources into one client field, so later credential injection cannot tell whether the profile is authoritative.
semantic_action.post_state: An authoritative-profile marker is present only for an explicit option or scoped request environment; the client may still receive an ambient profile through the fallback lookup without marking it authoritative.
semantic_action.validation: Capture client configuration for explicit, scoped, and ambient-only profiles; explicit and scoped inputs must be recognized as precedence-bearing, while ambient-only profile discovery must retain the distinct behavior demonstrated by the access-key fallback test.

candidate_atomics.name: guard-lower-priority-credential-injection
candidate_atomics.title: Suppress lower-priority access keys when an authoritative profile is selected
candidate_atomics.description: Conditionally omit direct access-key credentials when an explicit or stored/scoped profile should control SDK credential resolution, while preserving access-key and skip-auth fallback behavior outside that condition.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent ambient access keys from silently overriding a deliberately selected credential profile without disabling valid access-key fallback.
semantic_action.pre_state: A complete access-key pair is always assigned as explicit client credentials when authentication is enabled, even when an authoritative profile has been selected.
semantic_action.post_state: Explicit client credentials are assigned only when authentication is enabled, a complete access-key pair exists, and no authoritative profile marker exists; otherwise the selected profile remains available to the SDK credential chain.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the mocked client constructor configuration: explicit or scoped profile plus ambient keys must omit credentials; keys without an authoritative profile must remain populated, including the ambient-profile-plus-keys case.

candidate_workflows.name: restore-explicit-credential-source-precedence
candidate_workflows.title: Restore deliberate credential selection without breaking ambient fallback
candidate_workflows.description: Trace the provenance of a selected profile into the runtime client, preserve that provenance as an authoritative marker, and use it to prevent lower-priority ambient keys from becoming explicit client credentials. Validate both the repaired conflict and unaffected fallback cases.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure a deliberately selected credential profile controls authentication when ambient access keys coexist, while retaining ambient credential behavior when no deliberate profile selection exists.
when_to_use: A client configuration can contain both a profile selector and directly injected credentials, and the SDK gives the direct credentials higher precedence.
Authentication resolution carries a request-explicit or stored/scoped profile into the provider runtime while ambient access keys may also be visible.
anti_goals: Do not disable ambient access-key authentication when no authoritative profile was selected.
Do not treat a merely ambient profile as equivalent to a request-explicit or stored/scoped selection.
Do not alter bearer-token selection, skip-auth dummy credentials, region selection, endpoint selection, or proxy behavior.
not_applicable_when: Credential sources cannot coexist or the downstream client does not give directly supplied credentials precedence over profile-based resolution.
The failure concerns bearer-token authentication, disabled signing, incomplete access-key pairs, or credential-store persistence rather than profile-versus-key precedence.
There is no evidence that the selected profile reaches the provider request options.
inputs: Provider-resolved scoped environment, including any stored profile
Ambient profile and access-key environment values
workflow_graph.entry_state: A deliberate profile can reach the runtime, but a complete ambient access-key pair is independently injected as explicit credentials and can override that profile.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Explicit or stored/scoped profiles suppress lower-priority direct access-key injection; access keys remain injected when no authoritative profile exists, including when the profile value is only ambient.

steps.condition: Apply when profile values may originate from request-explicit, stored/scoped, or ambient sources.
steps.validation: Confirm that explicit options and scoped request environment produce the authoritative marker, while ambient lookup remains only a fallback for the client profile field.

steps.condition: Apply when authentication is enabled and a complete access-key pair is available alongside possible profile configuration.
steps.validation: Captured client config omits credentials for explicit/scoped profiles and retains them for no-profile and ambient-profile-only cases.

validation_ladder: Verify the authentication call path stores a selected profile in scoped credential environment and merges it into request options.
Verify the implementation distinguishes explicit/scoped profile provenance from ambient profile discovery before building client credentials.
Run the focused mocked-client tests for explicit profile plus keys and scoped profile plus keys; both must omit direct credentials.
Run fallback cases with keys and no profile, then keys with only an ambient profile; both must retain direct credentials.
stop_conditions: Stop if profile provenance cannot be preserved through the authentication and request-option call path.
Stop if omitting direct credentials would leave the client without a usable profile or another SDK credential-chain source.
Stop if regression coverage does not include both the repaired precedence conflict and the unaffected ambient fallback cases.
